nodes.name: Validate Payload
nodes.notes: Expects the FlowPilot webhook POST body (nested under the Webhook node's .body) shaped as: { request_id, plan_id, action_id, action: { tool: 'email', operation: 'send_email', parameters: { to: string[], subject, body } } }. `to` must already be resolved, real addresses - never a name or team reference. Outputs { to, subject, text } consumed by the Send Email node below.

nodes.name: Send Email
nodes.notes: Bind your own SMTP credential here (Credential to connect with). No credential is exported with this workflow on purpose - a placeholder credential id makes the node LOOK configured while silently failing to resolve, which previously produced a false success (see 'Verify Send Result').

nodes.name: Verify Send Result
nodes.notes: Success is PROVEN, never assumed. Only an item carrying a real SMTP messageId is allowed to reach Respond Success. Both of Send Email's outputs feed in here, so a node error that passes its input straight through (which is what happens when the credential cannot be resolved) can never be reported as a successful send.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { success: true, message_id: $json.messageId, accepted: $json.accepted, message: "Email sent successfully" } }}

={{ { success: false, error_code: "EMAIL_SEND_ERROR", message: $json.error?.message || "The Send Email node did not return an SMTP message id, so the email was NOT sent. Check that an SMTP credential is bound to the Send Email node." } }}
={{ { success: false, error_code: "INVALID_PAYLOAD", message: $json.error?.message || "The request payload was invalid." } }}
